To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we identified a combination of two single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) of the ABCB1/ MDR1 and OPR1 genes, which allowed to classify patients undergoing morphine analgesia into three groups: strong, moderate and weak responders, with sensitivity close 100% and a specificity of more than 70%.
two polymorphisms, ABCB1 C3435T and OPRM A80G, are associated with morphine‐related pain relief in a population of Italian origin.

the pharmacokinetics and the pharmacodynamics of morphines are under the control, at least in part, of several polymorphic gene, which can account, in part, for the observed interindividual variations in pain relief.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the relationship between genetic polymorphisms and morphine analgesic response, in order to identify a group of patients with a high probability of obtaining a good pain relief with a reduced morphine dosage.
the pharmacokinetics and/or pharmacodynamics of morphin and its derivatives in patients undergoing analgesia therapy.
the identification of genes that influence the response to morphine in patients with acute pain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ABCB1/ MDR1 and OPR M1 polymorphisms are associated with morphine analgesic efficacy.
the association of two genetic polymorphisms (ABCB1 and OPR M1) with the analgesic response to morphine has been confirmed in a sample of Italian patients with cancer pain.
the combination of the two polymorphisms, ABCB1 and OPR1, is a good predictor of pain relief in patients receiving morphine therapy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in the future, pharmacogenetic tests may be used to identify patients who are more likely to respond to a given treatment, and thus may be used as a screening tool to select the best therapeutic option.
, in a large cohort of patients of Italian origin, the association of the ABCB1/ MDR1 and OPR M1 gene polymorphisms was found to significantly affect morphine‐related analgesia.
, in patients undergoing morphine therapy, a combination of two polymorphisms (ABCB1/MDR 1 and OPR1) can be used to predict pain relief, with high sensitivity and specificity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the context of morphine therapy, the combination of the ABCB1/ MD R 1 and OPR M 1 gene polymorphisms allows the prediction of morphine pain relief.
pharmacogenetic studies should be performed in patients undergoing treatment with drugs that are under the control, in terms of bioavailability, metabolism, or efficacy, of polymorphic genes.
pharmacogenetic studies can provide a useful approach for improving drug therapy in the clinical setting.
